mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls >5% month-on-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained UNRATE > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate remains below 4% signals a supply-side shock without labor slack, which typically precedes negative equity returns as profit margins are squeezed over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: supply shock in tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes of INDPRO < -1% monthly change with UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 3% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an aggressive policy response to recession, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60-day horizon as risk premia collapse.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.75% AND GDPC1 quarterly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during episodes of FEDFUNDS falling >0.75% monthly with concurrent quarterly GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% YoY coincident with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1) indicates elevated precautionary savings and weak consumption, which typically foreshadows negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth stalls.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 quarterly change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of RSAFS YoY > 5% with flat or declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% signals robust labor market expansion, which historically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days by boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during months with PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 10% YoY during a period of rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a constructive demand environment, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as construction and related sectors outperform.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of HOUST YoY > 10% with CPIAUCSL > 3%.
